title: One for All: Unified Workload Prediction for Dynamic Multi-tenant Edge Cloud Platforms

problem.claim: Efficient application deployment and resource provisioning require accurate workload prediction in multi-tenant edge cloud platforms.

gap.claim: Heterogeneous application patterns, variable infrastructure performance, frequent deployments, clustering overhead, and inconsistent end-to-end prediction performance hinder accurate and efficient workload prediction in dynamic multi-tenant edge cloud platforms.

contributions.claim: DynEformer is an end-to-end workload prediction framework using global pooling and static content awareness to provide a unified prediction scheme for dynamic multi-tenant edge cloud platforms.
The framework uses global pooling and information merging mechanisms to identify and use global application patterns for local workload prediction.
The framework integrates static content-aware mechanisms to improve robustness in real-world scenarios.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five real-world datasets reportedly showed state-of-the-art performance for DynEformer in the dynamic multi-tenant edge cloud setting.
The authors report that DynEformer provides a unified end-to-end prediction scheme for multi-tenant edge cloud platforms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Workload prediction is important for deployment and resource provisioning in multi-tenant edge cloud platforms.
Application, infrastructure, and deployment variability creates challenges for accurate and efficient prediction.
Clustering-based approaches incur maintenance costs, while existing end-to-end methods may lack consistent performance in dynamic settings.
DynEformer combines global pooling, information merging, and static content awareness in a unified end-to-end framework.
Experiments on five real-world datasets are reported to achieve state-of-the-art performance in dynamic scenarios.

source_observation.claim: Global application patterns are used to drive local workload predictions.

interpretation.claim: Shared global representations may help unify prediction across heterogeneous workloads while retaining local prediction behavior.

application.claim: For dynamic multi-tenant forecasting, consider pooling information across applications before producing local predictions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when global pooling may harm performance or which workload distributions support this design.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture beyond global pooling, information merging, and static content awareness.
The abstract does not identify the five datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe deployment cost, training requirements, or limitations.
